market_holds: Spot 20.02 at the 2026-11-23 seal (sealed baseline), -7.8% over 5 sessions, -10.0% over 20 and -40% from the 52-week high. Yahoo daily bars show 23.05 on 11-12 falling to 19.27 on 11-20, a 16.4% drop over six sessions on 2-3x normal volume (1.13M shares on 11-20, the November options expiry), then a bounce to about 20.1 today. I found no company filing, rating change or news that explains that drop. The likely causes are tax-loss season and the warm-winter (strong El Nino) narrative after CPC's 11-19 update. The front-expiry straddle implies a 10.46% event move with a 45%-of-mid ATM spread, so the figure is indicative only. Over the last 7 prints the median absolute reaction was 13.8% and 5 of 7 were down (-14.6, +6.7, -14.8, -13.8, -10.7, +26.2, -5.8). For FQ4 the consensus is about a $0.01 loss on $221M of revenue (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-15). The FY26 EBITDA guide is a $230M midpoint, with salt at $225-236M after cuts and plant nutrition raised to $49-57M. The line the stock will trade on is the first FY27 guide, which has no published consensus. One undated aggregator shows FY27 EBITDA near $252M. Management has pre-framed that guide: bid-season price up about double digits, a deliberately lower committed volume, normal-weather assumptions, and Goderich unit costs still above plan. A capital allocation update is also promised. The tape already holds two known items. The Morton Fairport Harbor mine shutdown (10-26) coincided with CMP gaining about 8% from 10-23 to 10-27. The warm-fall and El Nino outlook coincided with the November slide. Sentiment in the previews is described as 'modestly bearish'. Short interest was about 4.9% of float on 2026-09-30 (an aggregator, not FINRA).
view: This print is mostly about the FY27 guide and how credible it looks. Management has told the market what goes into it: about +10% on highway price from a tight bid season (Q3 call, 2026-08-06), lower committed tons while it rebuilds inventory, Goderich costs that 'have not come down the way we expected', and a normal-weather assumption. Two things since August help the setup. Salt was excluded from the Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods (company statement, 2026-09-10), which removes a Goderich cost risk. Morton's Fairport Harbor mine flooded and shut on 2026-10-26, taking supply out of the Great Lakes market where CMP sells. The stock already rallied about 8% on the Morton news, though, and has since given back about 16%. Against those, three things weigh. CMP's guide and Goderich updates have repeatedly disappointed (down 10-15% on 4 of the last 5 prints). FY27 Q1 (Oct-Dec) is starting into what may be a record-warm fall and a very strong El Nino, which management will have to address on the 09:00 ET call before the open. And the accounting function turned over in October, after material weaknesses were flagged earlier. The pre-print slide looks like expectations being reset rather than information I can identify. That makes a normal-weather guide with price-led EBITDA growth able to produce a relief move. It does not make one likely enough to bet on, because the Goderich cost line and the volume commitment are exactly where this management has missed. The two sides roughly cancel. I see a large move with no edge on direction, tilted very slightly down by the reaction history and the weather.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line is the FY27 salt EBITDA guide, and its pieces (about +10% price, lower committed tons, sticky Goderich costs, normal weather) were pre-announced in August. The two newer facts, the tariff exclusion and the Morton outage, both coincided with visible price moves. The 16% slide into the print looks like a reset of expectations, not hidden information. I cannot show a gap between the price and what the release will reveal, so I make no recommendation.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY27 salt EBITDA guide clearly above about $260M with a credible Goderich unit-cost step-down, plus a buyback in the capital allocation update, would make me long. A guide at or below FY26's roughly $230M salt, or another delay or cost increase on the Goderich mill, would make me short.

self_critique: The case for long: the stock fell 16% into the print without news, at the bottom of its range and at about 6.5x FY26 EBITDA (my arithmetic from about 42M shares and $660M net debt). The bid-season price increase is mechanical and contracted. Tariff relief and a competitor's mine outage both cut against the bear case, and a normal-weather guide will show EBITDA growth that tax-loss sellers did not wait for. A buyback could add a catalyst. The case for short: this management has disappointed on 4 of the last 5 prints for 10-15% each time, always on Goderich costs or guide quality. A warm start to FY27 Q1 will be discussed before the open. Lower committed tons put the burden on costs that have not fallen. Either side could be right; I cannot tell which with 65% confidence.
approach_notes: P4 (show it is priced) helped most. Reading the daily bars tied both newer positives to visible moves rather than assuming they were priced. P3 'freshest data first' surfaced the Morton outage and the tariff exclusion, which the preview got wrong (it treats the tariffs as live). With no dated FY27 consensus, P7's mechanism test could not be met; a playbook note on how to treat a first-time annual guide with no bar would help.
